{{Navbar-GOGPT-tracker}}
'''Avon power station''' is an operating power station of at least 670-megawatts (MW) in Ballito, Kwazulu-Natal, South Africa.

==Background==

The plant started operation in July 2016 after a 30-month construction period.<ref name='ref_M'>{{cite web |url=https://peakers.com/avon.html |title=peakers.com/avon.html |date= |access-date= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210907232754/https://peakers.com/avon.html |archive-date=September 7, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref> It was built with the intention to be converted to natural gas and combined cycle technology.<ref name='ref_J'>{{cite web |url=https://hulisani.co.za/project/avon-and-dedisa-peaking-power |title=Avon and Dedisa Peaking Power Investment - Hulisani Investment Opportunity - SA |date=September 1, 2019 |access-date=January 29, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210907231949/https://hulisani.co.za/project/avon-and-dedisa-peaking-power |archive-date=September 7, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>https://www.powermag.com/press-releases/avon-peaking-power-south-africas-largest-ipp-reaches-commercial-operation-adding-670-mw-to-the-national-grid/</ref>

Together with [[Dedisa power station|Dedisa Power Station]], with a combined capacity of 1005 MW,  the privately owned power plants supply power to Eskom under with 15-year Power Purchase Agreements (“PPA).”<ref name='ref_J'>{{cite web |url=https://hulisani.co.za/project/avon-and-dedisa-peaking-power |title=Avon and Dedisa Peaking Power Investment - Hulisani Investment Opportunity - SA |date=September 1, 2019 |access-date=January 29, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210907231949/https://hulisani.co.za/project/avon-and-dedisa-peaking-power |archive-date=September 7, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref>
